The petitioner has filed this petition U/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.12.2022.
2.

The petition averments in brief are as under:
On 05.12.2022 at about 2.15 p.m., the petitioner was traveling as a passenger in a BMTC bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581 on Vidyaranyapura main road and at that time the left back side tyre blasted due to which, the metal sheet hit to the petitioner on Durgappa Madar Alias Durgappa Y. sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Soukya hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Aveksha Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident,
petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as canter driver and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent is the owner and internal insurer of the bus is liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

3. After service of notices respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of BMTC bus bearing No. KA-01-F- 9581.
Further denied the age, avocation, alleged disability and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
the respondent prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of BMTC bus bearing Reg. No. KA-01- F_9581 by its driver, in RTA took place on 5.12.2022 at about 2.15 p.m. on Vidyaranyapura main road, near Madeshwara Tiffin, Vidyaranyapura, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, at what rate and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 13.
Also examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3, through them got marked Ex.P14 to 23.
The driver of the bus is examined as RW.1 and document Ex.R1 is marked.
6. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

Issue No.1 : In the affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the affirmative
Issue No.3 :

sentences.text: That by reiterating all the averments made in the petition, the petitioner has filed his affidavit in lieu of- examination in-chief, which is considered as P.W.1.

In support of his case, he has produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, IMV report, wound certificate,
charge sheet, notice issued to owner of the vehicle and reply issued by him which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 7.
9.
On perusal of Ex.P1, FIR is registered on the basis of the first information.

Ex.P2 first information is given by the wife of the petitioner by alleging the negligence act of the driver of bus bearing No.
KA-01-F- 9581.

The contents of Ex.P2 complaint and Ex.P1 FIR supports the contention of the petitioner against the negligence driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01- F-9581 which is owned and insured by the respondent.
In continuation of Ex.P1 & 2, the police drawn spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P3.
At the time of Ex.P3, the rough sketch is also drawn by the police.

It is very important to note that in the written statement of the respondent, the respondent admitted the incident but denied the part of negligence by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581.
10.

It is admitted by the respondent that the petitioner was traveling in the bus bearing No.
KA-01-F- 9581 and also admitted that the back side left tyre has got burst and due to the said blast the steel sheets of the bus got into the right leg of the petitioner and got fractures.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner due to the said tyre blast is admitted by the respondent.
11. Only point for consideration in this case is whether the said tyre blast is due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01- F-9581?
Or it is due to the mechanical defect.
As per Ex.P4 IMV report, the bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581 the front portion of the right side rear wheel mud guard metallic body is damaged.
The Ex.P4 also reveals that the break systems are in order and the accident is not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.

It is the allegation of the petitioner that the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581 was driving the said bus in rash and negligent manner and due to his rash and negligent driving, the tyre of the said bus has got blast.
In this regard, as per Ex.P4 there is no mechanical defects are found by the Sr. Inspector of Motor Vehicles.
PW.1 who was traveling as a passenger and there is no contributory negligence by the petitioner or by the other vehicle for the said incident.
The driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F- 9581 examined himself as RW.1 and deposed by denying the rash and negligent driving.

When the RW.1/
the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581cross-xamined by the learned counsel for the petitioner,
he admitted that before taking out the bus usually they will check the condition of the bus.

In this case, if the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581 has verified the condition of the tyres before taking out the said bus is believed to be true, then what is the reasons for blasting of tyre when there is no mechanical defects are found by the IMV inspector as per Ex.P4- IMV report.
12. The tyre has got blast and the driver who is on the duty of verifying the said bus before taking the said bus for plying is the sole concern for the occurrence of said accident.

sentences.text: Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a Civil Court.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

14. Hence, by relying on the said precedent and in the absence of rebuttal evidence and denial in respect of police documents marked at Ex.P1 to 7, this court is of the opinion that the accident has happened due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581.
15.

In a claim for compensation under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319 Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others.

The respondent being the owner has not stated any grounds which caused the injuries to the petitioner except denying the case of the petitioner.

In this context by considering the contents of Ex.P1 to 7 this court tilts in favour of the petitioner as the petitioner has to prove the alleged negligence on the basis of the evidence and proof of the same on preponderance of probabilities.

The Ex.P 6 charge sheet also supports the view of this court, as the charge sheet filed for the offence punishable under Sec. 279 & 338 of IPC against the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01-F-9581.
19.
As per well settled principle of law, the standard of proof in the claim petition like the present is preponderance of the probability.
There are no grounds to disbelieve the case of petitioner in the absence of rebuttal evidence.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 08.11.2019 which is caused by the driver of the the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01- F-9581 which belonging to respondent.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2:
20.
As already held herein above, the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the driver of BMTC bus bearing No. KA-01- F-9581 belongs to respondent.
Hence, the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be ascertained on different heads.

The petitioner examined Medical Record Technician/ incharge at Aveksha Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P14 to 21.
a) PAIN AND AGONY :
- At the time of alleged accident the petitioner was aged about 28 years.
The petitioner has produced Aadhaar card at Ex.P9 also shows that the petitioner was aged about 28 years at the time of accident.

In the petition itself he has averred that immediately after the accident he was admitted to Soukya Hospital and after first aid he was shifted to Aveksha Hospital wherein he was admitted as inpatient from on 05.11.2022 and discharged on 12.12.2022.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 & 18 the petitioner sustained right tibia distal third commiunted fracture ( open GA type II) and extensor tendon injury of right great toe.
He underwent ORIF with IM nailing of right tibia + Extensor tendon repair done under SA on 5.12.2022.
If we perused the evidence of the doctor certainly the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate is causing a considerable disability to the petitioner.
As per X-ray dated 6.10.2023 the tibia with implants in situ is mal united and the distal fibula is non united.
No other evidence is placed by the respondent to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.
The mal united and non union of fractures has greater effects over the future life and earning capacity of the injured.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Rs.40,000/- may be awarded to the petitioner under this head.

5 b)
Medical expenses:
The petitioner has produced 25 medical bills as per Ex.P10, amounting to Rs.8,131/-.
The respondent produced Ex.R1 by stating that they have paid Rs.1,14,795/- towards the medical expenses directly to the Aveksha Hospital.
On perusal of the medical bills marked at Ex.P10 the petitioner produced OPD bill receipts and pharmacy bills, no inpatient bill is produced by the petitioner.

As such, the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the bill produced at Ex.P.10 and the payment of Rs.1,14,795/- made by the respondent towards the medical expenses is also covered under this head and remaining amount of Rs.8,131/- is to be payable by the respondent.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case in combined with the alleged injuries the petitioner is entitle for the reimbursement of the same by rounding of the same i.e., Rs.8,200/-.
c) Loss of income during laid up period:
The petitioner has stated that he was working as canter driver and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
To prove the said fact the petitioner has not produced any document.
To consider the avocation of the petitioner except the oral evidence, no documents or proof of salary is shown by the petitioner.
Such being the case it is just and necessary to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,500/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2022.
As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8- the petitioner was admitted to Aveksha Hospital on 5.12.2022 and discharged on 12.12.2022 for 8 days.

Thereafter usually the healing period has to be considered for which in the absence of evidence this court is of the opinion that in total two months may be considered under this head as a loss of income.

So, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,500 X 2= Rs.31,000/- during the laid up period.
d) Disability;- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by him the petitioner examined Dr.S.A.
Somashekara Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, as PW.3, through him outpatient record and X-ray are marked under Ex.P.22 & 23.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained Type II open # comminuted (Rt) distal tibia and fibula + extensor tendon injury of (Rt) great toe.
He underwent ORIF with IMIL nailing of (Rt) tibia + extensor tendon repair done under SA on 5.12.2022.
He examined the petitioner for assessment of disability.
Petitioner suffered disability of right lower limb at 50% and whole body disability at 25%.
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
According to the petitioner he was working as driver of canter.
In the Ex.P2 at the time of registration of FIR the wife of the petitioner given the details of the petitioner as canter driver.
The petitioner produced Ex.P9- notarised copy of his Aahdar card and driving licence wherein the petitioner has valid driving licence to drive transportation vehicle.
The petitioner pleaded that he was earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
But no documents is produced by the petitioner to show his exact income.

As per Ex.P8- discharge summary and Ex.P5 wound certificate and as per the injuries mentioned at point No.1 & 2 of wound certificate, the petitioner has got injuries in his right leg and also middle third of right leg.
If we perused the evidence of the doctor certainly the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate is causing a considerable disability to the petitioner.
As per X-ray dated 6.10.2023 the tibia with implants in situ is mal united and the distal fibula is non united.
No other evidence is placed by the respondent to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.
The mal united and non union of fractures has greater effects over the future life and earning capacity of the injured.

By considering the same this court is of the opinion that the disability would Durgappa Madar Alias Durgappa Y. Madar vs B.M.T.C on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59626913/
6 be 20% in this case by considering the age and avocation of the petitioner.

sentences.text: As per the Aadhar card marked at Ex.P9, as per this document the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 01.06.1994.
The accident was occurred in the year-2022.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 28 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of petitioner is '17'.

Hence, I inclined to award future loss of income at Rs.15,500/- X 12 X 17 X 20% =Rs.6,32,400/- which is the total loss of future income.
e) FOOD, NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE ;
As per Ex.P8 & 18 discharge summaries, the petitioner took treatment as inpatient for a period of 8 days.
As per the wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous and simple in nature.
If we perused the evidence of the doctor certainly the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate is causing a considerable disability to the petitioner.
As per X-ray dated 6.10.2023 the tibia with implants in situ is mal united and the distal fibula is non united.
No other evidence is placed by the respondent to disbelieve the evidence of the doctor in this regard.
The mal united and non union of fractures has greater effects over the future life and earning capacity of the injured.

By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
f) ATTENDANT CHARGES:
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
The petitioner was admitted as inpatient for 8 days in the hospital and there is no evidence or pleading in this regard to show that the petitioner is in need of attendant.

But by considering the nature of the grievous injuries as discussed above, one month of healing period including the inpatient period may be considered to award attendant charges at Rs.1,000/- per day i.e., Rs.30,000/- in total.

g) Towards loss of amenities and enjoyment of life:
The petitioner admitted to the hospital for the injuries sustained by him, which might certainly have deprived him of the basic comforts and enjoyment.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award a reasonable sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
h) Towards future medical expenses:
PW.3 in his affidavit evidence has stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which may costs Rs.30,000/-.
Hence, by looking to the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him, I inclined to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
a) Towards pain and agony Rs. 40,000/-
b) Towards medical expenses Rs. 8,200/-

21. Liability:-
According to the petitioner the respondent is the owner and there is a internal insurance to the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
22.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.8,11,600/- (Rupees Eight lakhs eleven thousand six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment on his proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.

All the materials available on record leading to show that, petitioner has sustained injuries in the accident took place on 08.11.2019 which is caused by the driver of the the driver of bus bearing No. KA-01- F-9581 which belonging to respondent.
There is no reasons to discard the evidence of petitioner.
In the claim petition like present one strict proof is not necessary but preponderance of probabilities is sufficient.
The mal united and non union of fractures has greater effects over the future life and earning capacity of the injured.
By considering the nature of the injuries and period he spent to overcome the pain and other allied effects of the accident Hence looking to the treatment taken by the petitioner and injuries sustained he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards food and nourishment, conveyance.
The petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.8,11,600/- (Rupees Eight lakhs eleven thousand six hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner, 50% of the same to be released in favour of petitioner through E-payment on his proper identification and remaining 50% to be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
